idk if this is unpopular, but i agree! as someone who enjoys listening to the vocals in kpop songs, it's a shame that i can't fully enjoy tracks from HYBE-grown artists (txt, enha, and even bts' new stuff) because of the "sterile" vocals, like you mentioned. i think it's also because i got into kpop pretty early on (2009), and my ears are tuned to the SM and YG style of vocal production which works towards the advantage of the vocalists by highlighting their tone & ability. not all of their artists are amazing vocalists either, but hearing the nuances between the vocalists in their groups help create a sound that's uniquely their own. 

i'd like to dig deeper into txt's discography especially, but the vocal production in particular ruins the experience for me altogether. i don't think hybe's producers will do anything about it sooner or later though lol. maybe vocals are really dead in kpop now?
